dublinCore.title: Phasor Addition
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Phasors
Euler's formula
Sinusoidal signals
Complex numbers
Beats
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that adds up to three sinusoids A_k cos(w t + phi_k) by adding their phasors A_k e^{j phi_k} head to tail. A rotating phasor diagram (blue real axis, red imaginary axis, green resultant) sits beside the individual waveforms and their sum with a cursor at the current time; read-outs give the resultant amplitude and phase. A second-frequency mode lets phasor 2 turn at f2, so the resultant length becomes the envelope of a beating signal at |f2 - f1|.

searchKeywords: adding sinusoids of the same frequency

learningObjectives: Calculate the resultant phasor R = sum of A_k e^{j phi_k} for up to three sinusoids of one frequency and write their sum as |R| cos(w t + angle R)
Predict from the phase difference whether two sinusoids reinforce, partly cancel or cancel completely, using |R| = 2A|cos(delta phi / 2)| for equal amplitudes
Demonstrate with the speed slider that the resultant amplitude and phase do not depend on the rotation rate w when every phasor shares that frequency
Relate the projection of the rotating resultant onto the real axis to the value of the summed waveform at the cursor
Analyze the sum of two sinusoids at different frequencies as a resultant whose length changes with time, and calculate the beat frequency |f2 - f1| and the envelope range
prerequisites: Complex numbers in rectangular and polar form
Amplitude, frequency and phase of a sinusoid

misconceptions.misconception: The amplitudes of two sinusoids add
misconceptions.correction: Only phasors that point the same way add their lengths; in general |R| is the length of the vector sum
misconceptions.evidence: At the default settings 1.00 at 0 degrees plus 1.00 at 90 degrees gives R = 1.41, and the thick green sum peaks at 1.41, not 2

misconceptions.misconception: The phase of the sum is the average of the individual phases
misconceptions.correction: The phase is the angle of the vector sum; it equals the average only when the amplitudes are equal
misconceptions.evidence: With A1 = 2.00 at 0 degrees and A2 = 1.00 at 90 degrees the read-out shows R = 2.24 at 26.6 degrees, not 45 degrees

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Phasor addition. Left: up to three rotating phasors, drawn head to tail in orange, purple and brown, and their green resultant on a complex plane with a blue real axis and a red imaginary axis. Right: each phasor's cosine waveform as a thin line and their sum as a thick green line over an 8 second window, with a gold cursor at the current time. Sliders set each amplitude and phase, the rotation frequency f1 and a second frequency f2 for phasor 2; read-outs give the resultant amplitude and phase, or the beat frequency.

controls.label: Play / Pause
controls.description: Starts and stops the rotation and the time cursor (the sim opens paused)

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns to t = 0 and pauses, so every phasor sits at its phase angle

controls.label: Speed f1
controls.description: Rotation frequency f1 of the phasors (w1 = 2 pi f1)

controls.label: Phasor 2 at f2
controls.description: Lets phasor 2 turn at the second frequency f2 so the sum beats

controls.label: f2
controls.description: Second frequency used by phasor 2 when 'Phasor 2 at f2' is checked

visualElements.description: Rotating phasor diagram: phasors head to tail, green resultant, dashed circle traced by its tip, and a blue dot marking its projection on the real axis
Waveform plot over an 8 s window: thin individual waveforms, thick green sum, dashed envelope plus or minus |R(t)| and a gold time cursor
Read-out of R in polar and rectangular form, the sum as |R| cos(w1 t + angle R), the current time and value, w1; in beat mode the envelope range, beat frequency and beat period

model.description: Each phasor k turns as A_k e^{j(2 pi f_k t + phi_k)}; all share f1 except phasor 2 in second-frequency mode. The waveform is the real part. The resultant in the frame turning at f1, R(t) = sum A_k e^{j(phi_k + 2 pi (f_k - f1) t)}, is constant for one frequency and gives the envelope |R(t)| otherwise.
equations: sum A_k cos(w t + phi_k) = Re{(sum A_k e^{j phi_k}) e^{j w t}} = |R| cos(w t + angle R)
|R| = 2A |cos((phi2 - phi1)/2)| for two phasors of equal amplitude A
A cos(2 pi f1 t) + A cos(2 pi f2 t) has envelope 2A |cos(pi (f1 - f2) t)|
|R(t)| ranges from ||S| - A2| to |S| + A2, where S is the sum of the phasors at f1

instructionalStrategies: Predict the resultant before reading it
Compare the projection of the resultant with the summed waveform at the cursor
Contrast one-frequency sums with beating sums
extensions: Add a rotating-frame view in which same-frequency phasors stand still
Connect the sum of phasors to the addition of voltages in an AC circuit
